newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica seen weaker until September.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica seen weaker until September.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Telefonica will continue to retrace part of a strong outperformance earlier this year as long as a battle over digital television and a volatile trend in the overall bourse goes on, dealers said on Tuesday.

"Telefonica is still more or less moving with the market, but although there is some negative sentiment involving the wrangle over digital television, until the final outcome is known we can't really expect it to have a strong impact on the shares," said a trader at Banesto Bolsa in Madrid.
Telefonica hit an all-time closing high of 4,665 pesetas on July 7, a rise of 55 percent since the start of the year -- a period in which it consistently outstripped the Ibex-35 blue chip index.
At 1102 GMT, Telefonica was up 45 pesetas, 1.1 percent, to 4,055 while the Ibex-35 was 1.5 percent higher at 6,650.69.

"Telefonica has been weaker since it has been waiting for certain issues to be resolved. But after September we expect it to climb back up to 4,500 pesetas within two months. But of course the Ibex would have to recover to 7,100 for that to happen," the Banesto trader said.
Canal Satelite, a digital television platform competing with Telefonica's Via Digital, said on Monday it was willing to hold talks about sharing its exclusive football viewing rights.
But Via Digital rejected the offer on Tuesday, saying Canal Satelite did not have exclusive rights for the upcoming season.
Analysts say the football rights are key to the success of the digital television platforms, although it is not yet clear how the issue will be resolved.
Another trader at a local brokerage explained the performance of Telefonica in purely technical terms.
"On Telefonica, it's fatigue. It has reached a historical maximum through July and a correction period should be coming up," he said.
Share price weakness in Telefonica's international alliance partner BT was not for the moment seen having a major impact on the Spanish operator, dealers said.
Doubts about BT's merger with MCI has sometimes in the past weighed on Telfonica shares.
